_comment: Standing record of adversarial lead audits. gate.sh reads this so a green gate cannot coexist with an unsendable lead list. Update it only by running the audit again, never by hand.

audits.note: First audit. Six failure modes named: URL-prefix instead of operation; vendor-owned or generated SDK code; anchor on a declaration rather than a call; changed field absent from the repo; vendored dependency trees; line numbers from a different revision. All six gated.

Re-audit after gating all six. Same rate. The gates changed WHY leads die, not HOW OFTEN. Root cause named: verification proved co-location and never dependence. Ten of twenty leads were one cluster where the call sites matched correctly and the change still could not affect them, because removing a 204 while the 200 remains narrows the API rather than breaking it. Fixed at the findings level.

Third audit, after the verifier was rebuilt around a dependence proof (call reaching the operation by method and full path template; or a read of the changed field traced back to a vendor call). The proof chains were judged accurate in every case -- the paths, methods and operations were right. The leads are still wrong, for a reason the rebuild did not address: operation reachability was accepted as sufficient for a whole-schema removal, so a caller who reaches the operation but never reads the removed schema's fields is reported as affected. Seven of ten fell that way. This audit also found a FINDINGS defect no previous round had named, described below.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed.what: OpenAPI security is a list of ALTERNATIVES: [{A}, {B}] means A or B. Both the engine and the independent precision checker flattened it to a set of scheme names, so adding an alternative scored as breaking.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.evidence: Twilio DELETE /v2/Services/{Sid} went from [{accountSid_authToken}] to [{accountSid_authToken}, {access_token_bearer}]. Every existing caller kept working. Nine operations were scored breaking.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.why_it_survived: The checker shared the engine's mistake, so it agreed with it. That is precisely the failure a separate checker exists to prevent, and it means the earlier 86/86 claim was wrong for the security class.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed.status: Fixed in both, independently. A change is breaking only when some old alternative can no longer be satisfied. Re-measured: 84 breaking findings, 84/84 confirmed, zero undecidable.

standing.blocker: Operation reachability is accepted as proof for a whole-schema removal. A caller who reaches the operation but never reads any field of the removed schema is not affected, and seven of ten audited leads were exactly that. The fix is to resolve the removed schema to its leaf field names in the OLD spec and require a read of one of them, rejecting calls whose response is discarded.
standing.findings_precision: 79/79, zero undecidable, after correcting the security defect and the schema-relocation defect above (the earlier 84/84 counted 5 relocations that break no caller)
also_open: operation_reached() stops at the first affected operation with a hit, in list order, so an alphabetically earlier DELETE whose response is discarded wins over a GET whose response is deserialized. Rank by whether the response is consumed.

A lead's breaks_on names the finding's representative operation while its proof names the operation the file actually calls, with nothing stating the two are related. This misled three auditors who had the repo, the spec and the source in front of them.
standing.note: The findings engine is verified. The lead pipeline is not. Do not send outreach built on leads until an audit clears.
standing.blocker_fix_implemented: The prescribed fix is now in dependence.py: a schema_removed proof requires a read of one of the deleted schema's own field names, and field names too generic to mean anything cannot carry it. NOT YET AUDITED — lead_precision and sendable stay as they are until a fourth adversarial audit runs.

findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.what: A schema is an implementation detail of an operation; a caller only ever sees the operation. Diffing schemas in isolation cannot tell a field being DELETED from a field being MOVED between two schemas that compose into the same operation, and the second breaks nobody.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.evidence: OpenAI removed `ResponseProperties.reasoning` in this window while `POST /responses` accepted `reasoning` throughout — it moved to another arm of the same allOf. Found by running the new `apidrift scan` against Azure-Samples/python-openai-demos, which reported reasoning.py:38 as broken. Five of 84 breaking findings were this class (OpenAI 3, Stripe 2).
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.why_it_survived: measure_precision.py asked the schema-level question — 'is the field still in this schema?' — which is the same question the engine asked, so it agreed. Identical shape to the security OR-of-AND defect above.
findings_defect_found_and_fixed_2.status: Fixed in both, independently. The engine suppresses a removal when every affected operation still exposes the name; the checker now resolves each affected operation from the RAW document with its own resolver and refutes relocations on its own. Mutation-verified: with the engine's suppression disabled, the checker independently refutes exactly those 5 (23/28 = 82.1%).
